Choose a plural form

Source: R/format.R
plural.Rd

The R form of an n span (rule 3.2.1): plural(n, "a person", "# people"). Arms are separate arguments, in the order a span writes them (rule 3.2.2): one arm is a template for #; two are one and other; three are zero, one and other; four are zero, one, two and other. # stands for the governor as printed by the default governor class. || and ## are a literal | and #; a backslash before either is removed.

Usage

plural(n, ...)

Arguments

n

A single number, or a weft_text from a formatter (selection then uses its printed record). A vector or a string is an error of class weft_value_error that says to write length(x); a missing value is an error of class weft_no_value.

...

One to four arms, as strings.

Value

A character vector of length one.

Examples

plural(1, "a person", "# people")
#> [1] "a person"
plural(3, "a person", "# people")
#> [1] "3 people"
plural(0, "never", "once", "twice", "# times")
#> [1] "never"
